value.name: Rosa explains the house should stay undivided
value.description: Rosa argues that the house should belong to one person rather than be split into three shares, framing the codicil as a legal formality and the conversation as a family wish.
evidence: sure of that is for the house to belong to one of you and not to be divided into three pieces of which one piece is mine. The codicil was for the law. This conversation is for the wish. Do you understand.

value.name: Lucia rejects Rosa's proposal
value.description: Lucia says she understands Rosa's point but refuses to accept it.
evidence: "I understand," Lucia said, "and I do not accept."

value.name: Rosa insists Lucia need not decide immediately
value.description: Rosa tells Lucia she does not have to accept the arrangement today, but Lucia repeats that she will not accept.
evidence: "You do not have to accept today."

value.name: Daniel interrupts Lucia
value.description: As Lucia begins to protest further, Daniel calls her name and interrupts the exchange.

value.name: Daniel asks Lucia to let Rosa finish
value.description: Daniel tells Lucia to let Rosa finish speaking and postpones disagreement until afterward.
evidence: "Lucia," Daniel said. He was looking at Rosa, not at his sister. "Let her finish. We can disagree with her in a minute. Let her finish what she is saying first."

value.name: Lucia falls silent
value.description: Lucia stops speaking in response to Daniel's intervention.

value.name: Rosa thanks Daniel
value.description: Rosa acknowledges Daniel's support with a brief thank-you, and he replies in kind.

value.name: Rosa ends her statement
value.description: Rosa declares that she is finished and invites the others to tell her she is wrong.
evidence: "I am finished," Rosa said. "That was what I had to say. Now you can tell me I am wrong."

value.name: Asha realizes she is only a witness
value.description: Asha recognizes that the discussion has shifted from legal procedure into family dynamics, leaving her outside the center of control for the first time since arriving.
evidence: She was, she realized, watching something she had not planned for and could not, in any formal sense, manage.
Rosa had taken the conversation out of the legal frame and placed it inside the family frame, and the family frame did not have rules of procedure, and Asha did not run it.
She was, for the first time since she had walked into this house on Monday morning, not the central figure in the room. She was a witness.

value.name: Asha sets down her pen and folds her hands
value.description: Asha responds by putting away her active note-taking posture and sitting back as a passive observer.
evidence: She picked up her pen, and she set it down, deliberately, on top of the single sheet of paper she had brought with her.
